name: strata-cut
title: Strata Cut
description: A pinned full-bleed drilling stage where scroll position is the depth of the bit: intact ground below the cutting front, cut borehole wall above it, and copy arriving as each stratum crosses the frame.
instruction: Build <StrataCut stages? pinLength? metresPerScreen? startDepth? bitLine? speed? children? className?> as a pinned, full-bleed scroll-driven story stage in which the scroll position IS the depth of a drill bit. DEPTH IS THE ONLY STATE: a sticky h-screen stage inside a tall section (pinLength * 100vh) computes progress = clamp(-rect.top / (rect.height - vh)), and every pixel's depth is bitDepth + (y - bitLine*H) * metresPerPixel. Default pinLength is 12 viewport heights, about 1.7 per stage, so one trackpad flick does not cross three of them. The image is a pure function of that one scalar, so scrolling back runs the bit back up the hole through exactly the ground it cut; nothing latches, accumulates or is 'reached'. THE FRAME IS SPLIT AT THE BIT LINE (default 0.3 of the height): below it the ground is intact and bedded in place, at it a cutting front with a bright working light, a dark kerf shadow and chip haze, above it the same strata seen as the cut cylinder wall of the borehole — cylindrically remapped (xw = asin(nx)/(pi/2) * halfWidth), lambertian on the curve, darkening up the hole away from the working light, tool-grooved by a helix whose pitch is set by depth, and veiled by cuttings flushing UPWARD whose advection speed rises with |descent rate|. Material therefore only ever moves one way through the frame and the state of any piece of ground is legible from where it sits. Above the collar (depth < 0) the hole opens into daylight with a bright broken rim; startDepth (2.4 m) puts the bit a couple of metres down at zero scroll so that daylight is a bright sliver at the top of the resting frame rather than a third of it, with the annulus below it already full of cuttings drifting up on the ambient clock. STRATA ARE GENERATED: a monotone depth warp u(d) = d/2.6 + 0.34*sin(d/2.6) has du/dd > 0 everywhere, so floor(u) is a bed index that cannot invert or pop however the depth is driven; per-bed luminance, lamination frequency, contact sharpness and clast density are hashed off that index, then biased toward a facies profile (lum, grain, structure) interpolated between the stage entries and passed as a vec4[8] uniform — so the bed under the copy that says 'peat seam' actually reads as one. Both sides of the bit line read the field in the SAME centred x metric, so the dip term cannot step a bed as it crosses the front, and every noise frequency, the lamina count and the contact sharpness are clamped against metres-per-pixel so no feature falls below ~2 css px and crawls while the column moves. Beds carry regional dip, a long undulation, fining-upward tone drift within each bed, anisotropic grain, jittered-grid clasts in coarse facies only, a dark parting at each contact whose sharpness is hashed (erosional vs gradational), and near-vertical joints crossing several beds. SCROLL HANDLING: the scroll position is read ONCE PER FRAME inside the rAF loop, never in a scroll handler, and the depth chases it with a 90ms exponential — a trackpad flick lands the target in one event burst and this is the whole reason the ground does not step with it. Native scrolling is never hijacked, so keyboard paging, space, Home/End and trackpad momentum all work by default; the sticky stage releases by ordinary layout at both ends with no boundary jump. A signed, smoothed descent rate drives the cutting front's intensity and the cuttings' flow speed, so stopping mid-column visibly stops the cut without freezing the frame. COPY: real DOM text, never rasterized. The accessible copy of the sequence is one sr-only ordered list in depth order, always present; the visual blocks are aria-hidden and driven by direct style writes (opacity, a small parallax offset, and a visibility toggle so seven backdrop-blur layers are not composited at once), never through React state, so scrolling never schedules a render. Under prefers-reduced-motion the depth snaps to the nearest stage (discrete states, no interpolation), the ambient clock freezes on a composed still, and copy switches instantly and stays fully readable. PALETTE: five luminance stops from --background, --foreground, --ns-muted and --border read via getComputedStyle and re-read on a documentElement class MutationObserver. --ns-accent never reaches the canvas — the column is achromatic in both themes and the ramp direction never inverts, only bias (+0.02 light, -0.06 dark) and contrast (1.22 / 1.18). HOST: an internal GLSurface owns the program, a fullscreen triangle pair and lazily-resolved uniform locations. DPR is capped at 2 with a wall-clock adaptive ladder (1, 0.72, 0.52) that steps down after ~0.9s over budget and climbs back on a doubling window; ResizeObserver resizes, an IntersectionObserver and visibilitychange stop the loop entirely when the stage is off screen or the tab is hidden, and webglcontextlost/restored rebuild cleanly.
useWhen: Pick strata-cut when a page needs a scroll section that advances a real, irreversible-looking physical process rather than a sequence of slides — the scroll axis is the depth axis, so scrolling back runs it backwards coherently. Pick a pinned gallery like gallery-gantry-track instead when the content is discrete items rather than a continuum, and weld-pool when you want a static full-bleed hero with no scroll coupling.
